reconstructed_theorem_text: For any probability measure pi on a finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space E, any reference point xref in E, and any real kappa at least one, assume the squared distance from xref is pi-integrable. Then the phase quadratic Kantorovich value between the product laws delta_xref tensor standard Gaussian and pi tensor standard Gaussian is at most the ordinary pi-integral of that squared distance, embedded in the extended nonnegative reals. The phase cost uses position coefficient 1/(2*kappa)+1/2, unit position-momentum cross term and unit momentum coefficient. The theorem claims neither an optimal coupling nor equality, and does not assert a numerical Gibbs or all-q bound.
objects: E, probability measure pi, point xref, real kappa, standard Gaussian momentum, the two product phase laws, and the phase quadratic Kantorovich value.
domains: A finite-dimensional complete real inner-product Borel space; laws on E and E times E; kappa is real.
quantifiers: Every probability pi, xref and kappa at least one, subject to the displayed finite second-moment assumption.
assumptions: The position law is a probability measure, the squared distance to xref is integrable, and kappa is at least one.
conclusion: The phase quadratic transport value of the specified initial and reference product laws is at most the position second moment about xref.
scopes: A q=2 squared-cost comparison for two specified product laws; no equality, optimizer, Gibbs specialization, all-q estimate, phase dynamics or query-cost claim.
constant_dependencies: The upper-bound coefficient is exactly one; kappa enters the underlying phase cost and its lower bound kappa at least one.
